articles.headline: NFL Week 12 arrivals: CeeDee Lamb leads arrivals ahead of Eagles-Cowboys
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.body:
The Thanksgiving menu includes an extra helping of NFL style, with Week 12 arrivals getting started before the turkey hits the table.

The Green Bay Packers visited the Los Angeles Rams on a warm Wednesday in Inglewood, California. 

Thursday brings the Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions together in Detroit, and morning temperatures in the 40s could lead to giving statement coats their moment. The Philadelphia Eagles visit the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, where a sunny afternoon in the 50s calls for sweater weather.

The Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night in Orchard Park, New York, to close out the tripleheader with temperatures in the 30s and rain in the forecast. Friday's meeting between the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh brings another opportunity for layers, with temperatures around the low 40s and possible showers.

Sunday offers a little of everything: jacket weather around the Great Lakes, warmer conditions in South Florida and potential rain in the Bay Area. Whether players are bundling up or keeping things breezy, there's plenty of room to serve a look.

Here are the standout arrivals from Week 12.

Thanksgiving threads

CeeDee Lamb donned a long black double-breasted overcoat, charcoal trousers and chunky lace-up boots. The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver accessorized with a leather tote and silver jewelry.

Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons embraced fall fashion in a camel-colored coat with plush shearling-style lapels, layered over a plum plaid suit and matching turtleneck. 

Wednesday's looks

Aaron Donald kept it sleek in a black zip-up jacket and matching pants, accessorizing with gold-tinted shades and a checkered designer pouch. His blue, white and yellow sneakers added a pop of Rams colors to the look.

articles.headline: Betting Broncos-Steelers: How will Pittsburgh respond to stunning events?
articles.description: Odds, analysis and recommended plays to help you bet the day after Thanksgiving game between the Broncos and Steelers.
articles.body:
Let's put Aaron Rodgers on Black Friday, the NFL thought. Think again!

Tuesday night's surprising news that the Pittsburgh Steelers were benching Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph -- and Rodgers' ensuing scorched-earth interview with Pat McAfee on Wednesday before then being cut by the team -- changed both the lineup and tenor of Friday's contest.

But despite the vibes being in a very different place between the 8-2 Denver Broncos and the 6-4 Steelers, these teams are not as far apart as one might think. The Broncos rank 15th and 14th in offensive and defensive EPA per play, respectively (with that defensive number being particularly surprising!). The Steelers rank 21st and 10th in the same categories. Just something to keep in mind as we turn our attention to picks for Friday's game.

Betting outlook

Here's an unconventional take from ESPN's Football Power Index: the Steelers' chance of winning Friday went up by benching Rodgers for Rudolph. Even outside of the Mike McCarthy/Rodgers drama, the reality of the situation is that Rodgers has played poorly in 2026 (as has been the case for years), with him ranking 26th out of 30 quarterbacks in QBR this year.

I would not go as far as FPI -- which makes this game almost a pick 'em with Rudolph at the helm -- because perhaps there's some truth to Rodgers' criticisms of McCarthy and his playcalling and also because I think that's an awful lot of confidence in Rudolph. If I had to pick a side (and, full disclosure, I almost never do), I suppose I would go Steelers +4.5. But I won't.

Instead, I'm going to think about tail outcomes here. What if things actually are as bad as Rodgers said? Or what if, even if exaggerated, the late quarterback switch and ensuing drama plays a big role in the team's preparation for Friday? Does that make a blowout loss more likely than a normal game? That seems possible to me. So let's play an alternate line and go Broncos -13.5 at +323.

Notable player props, bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Jonah Coleman receptions OVER 3.5 (+106)

We're employing one of my favorite betting angles here: running back reception overs against a zone-heavy team. Running backs catch passes against zone coverage 15% of the time, compared to just 8% of the time against man. That's a huge difference! In back testing I've found that that isn't fully captured by the market, so in extreme cases I believe it's worth betting. And this is an extreme case, because the Steelers run zone 78% of the time -- the most of any team.

articles.headline: Bears TE Colston Loveland ruled out vs. Lions with knee injury
articles.description: The Bears have ruled out tight end Colston Loveland for the rest of Thursday's game at Detroit with a left knee injury.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Bears tight end Colston Loveland has been ruled out for the rest of Chicago's Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Lions after injuring his left knee in the first quarter. 

Loveland was hurt while blocking on D'Andre Swift's 2-yard run on the Bears' second offensive series with 6:15 remaining in the quarter.

Loveland was engaged in a block with Lions linebacker Trevor Nowaske and got rolled up by linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez at the end of the play. He hobbled off the field under his own power and went to the medical tent for evaluation before being carted to the locker room with a towel over his head.

The Bears announced at the beginning of the second quarter that Loveland would not return. 

On the previous series -- Chicago's first drive of the game -- Loveland caught a 5-yard pass and made his way into the red zone before Detroit rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out from under Loveland's arm. It was the tight end's second lost fumble since Week 8 at Seattle.

The Bears were already thin at tight end after Cole Kmet sustained a season-ending knee injury late in Chicago's Week 7 win against the New England Patriots. Chicago's remaining active tight ends in Detroit are rookie Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson.

Loveland has 40 catches for 392 yards and three touchdowns through 10 games. He ranks third on the team in receiving yards.

articles.headline: Man United-linked Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds contract
articles.description: Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.
articles.body:
Leeds United have announced striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.

The 29-year-old has kick-started his career since leaving Everton as a free agent in 2025 to join Leeds on a three-year deal following their promotion back to the Premier League.

He scored 14 top-flight goals last season and has five in 11 appearances this term, while his form at Elland Road has seen him recalled to the England squad.

The deal comes amid reports that Man United were potentially interested in the striker.

"Leeds United are delighted to announce Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with the club," a statement said.

"The England international has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Elland Road, keeping him in West Yorkshire until the summer of 2029."

- Football's main character this week: Jude Bellingham is in a new stratosphere

- Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino

Large chunks of Calvert-Lewin's nine-year spell at Everton were blighted by injury, but he missed only three league games last season and has started in all 11 top-flight fixtures in the current campaign.

He won the Premier League's Player of the Month Award in December after scoring in six consecutive matches.

After being recalled by England for a 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay in March, Calvert-Lewin retained his place in Thomas Tuchel's squad for Nations League matches against Spain and Czechia.

His latest England appearance was against Spain earlier this month when he stepped off the bench to win his 15th cap in the Three Lions' 3-2 Nations League win.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL Thanksgiving preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
articles.description: Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills are still on deck. We have the top storylines, bold predictions, stats to know, fantasy/betting nuggets and more.
articles.body:
Holiday football is here, and the NFL started this season's Thanksgiving week slate a day earlier than normal. On Wednesday night, the Rams beat the Packers. But we have three great Thanksgiving Day games, too.

The Lions and Packers kicked it off, and an NFC East showdown between the Eagles and Cowboys is up next. And to conclude Thursday's games, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will visit Josh Allen and the Bills in the first clash of NFL MVPs on the holiday, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

Ahead of the matchups, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside each locker room with key storylines and a look back at each team's history playing on Thanksgiving. ESPN Research provides optimistic stats for every team, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. Plus, analytics writer Seth Walder makes bold predictions and fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and three analysts -- Maldonado, Moody and Walder -- give us final score picks for the games.

Eagles (3-7) at Cowboys (5-6)

Thursday, 4:30 p.m. ET | Fox | DAL -8.5 (47.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Eagles: With edge rusher Jonathan Greenard getting healthier and counterpart Nolan Smith Jr. continuing his surge, the Eagles have racked up 11 sacks and 15 QB hits over the past two games. "I've been telling you guys that it would come, but you didn't believe me," defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said of the pass rush. "But the guy we're playing this week [Dak Prescott] I think is the hardest guy in the league to sack." The cornerback room took some hits with Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) and Jonathan Jones (ankle) getting injured against Pittsburgh. Jones is expected to be sidelined against Dallas, but Fangio indicated Mitchell should be OK to play. Either way, if Philadelphia has any shot of slowing down Dallas, the front seven will have to continue its high level of play. -- Tim McManus

What we're hearing on the Cowboys: The Cowboys are not out of the NFC East picture yet, but they need to keep winning to apply pressure against the Giants. The Cowboys have not posted back-to-back wins since last Thanksgiving, and ex-Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton would love nothing more than to show off against a team that did not believe he was worthy of the backup job to Prescott. But the holiday game has been kind recently to the Cowboys, who have won four in a row. The last time they had a Thanksgiving winning streak that long was from 1980 to 1985. -- Todd Archer

Stat the Eagles are thankful for: In their Week 11 win over the Steelers, running back Saquon Barkley recorded a season-high 61 rushing yards before contact. He also increased his touchdown streak to a career-high four straight games.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Barça, Madrid jockey for position in Erling Haaland chase
articles.description: Barcelona and Real Madrid are positioning themselves for a move for Man City striker Erling Haaland. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Barcelona and Real Madrid have hopes of signing Manchester City star Erling Haaland next summer, while the Catalan club are interested in a loan move for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona and Real Madrid are manoeuvring behind the scenes over a move for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland in 2027, according to TEAMtalk. Both Spanish giants are in regular contact through intermediaries as they remain hopeful that they can engineer a move for the 26-year-old. Liverpool, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain have also shown an interest in Haaland, but they and senior figures at the Etihad are aware that the Norway international wants to test himself in LaLiga.

- Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move away from Manchester United, and Barcelona are interested in the center back, according to The Sun. The 20-year-old has been left on the bench in both of Mauricio Pochettino's matches since the Argentine took over at Old Trafford. Fulham are also interested in Heaven, with Calvin Bassey having been linked with a January move going the other way, although that is deemed unlikely due to the 26-year-old's importance to the Cottagers.

- Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur, Man City, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Juventus all had scouts watching Antonio Nusa as the winger scored a brace in RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over Lens, according to TEAMtalk. Atletico Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are also interested in the 21-year-old. Leipzig are aware of the growing interest in Nusa and are working on a potential new contract for the Norway international, whose existing deal runs until 2029.

- Liverpool, Manchester United and Newcastle United are all interested in Juventus winger Francisco Conceição, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. Jorge Mendes offered the 23-year-old to the Magpies for next June in a deal that could also allow Juve to permanently sign Nick Woltemade. Conceicao isn't thinking about his future and has even hinted at the possibility of staying with Juventus and trying to win trophies with the club.

- Napoli is the first club to make a move for Monza striker Gustavo Varela, but Juventus, AC Milan and Inter are also in the mix for the 21-year-old, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. There are also various Premier League clubs following Varela, while Como could look to him due to uncertainty around Moise Kean's injury situation. For Milan, Varela is seen as an alternative to Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi, while Inter would only move in the summer.

Other rumors

- Manchester United's interest in Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen has resurfaced. (TEAMtalk)

- Arsenal have added Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs to their list of options for the January transfer window. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool could trigger their option to re-sign Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah in 2027.

articles.headline: NFL Week 12 uniforms: Rams debut alternates, Cowboys rock Thanksgiving throwbacks
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 12, led by an alternate uniform for the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The NFL on Thanksgiving is a classic tradition, and the uniforms are as much a part of the games as a celebratory turkey leg. But, this year a game will be played on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time. And it's only right that the matchup included the debut of a uniform, too. 

The Los Angeles Rams wore their "Fearsome White" threads against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. The all-white look is inspired by the Rams' "Fearsome Foursome" defensive line from the 1960s and early 1970s. A modern "Rams Royal" lid includes white horns, white facemask, new 3D bumper logos and "Rams" on the front. Royal blue stripes run over the shoulder to mirror the curve of the helmet horn, alongside accenting sleeve numbers.

The fifth annual John Madden celebration will be held on Thanksgiving, and a patch featuring a silhouette of Madden will be included on the jersey of each player at all of the Wednesday and Thursday games.

A Thanksgiving tripleheader means throwback threads, led by the Dallas Cowboys rocking their 1960s-era uniforms against the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas brought this combination back in 2022 following a nine-year hiatus. The navy and white look includes a clean lid with a navy star on the side and a stripe down the middle. 

On Black Friday, the Pittsburgh Steelers are dressing for the occasion with their color rush threads against the Denver Broncos. The all-black look includes gold numbers and stripes on the sleeves, with a similarly colored stripe down the pants. Pittsburgh owns a 9-3 record in the uniform.

The holiday slate isn't the only place to find uniform heat. The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy ensemble against the New England Patriots. It's color rush week for the New Orleans Saints with an all-white combination versus the Cincinnati Bengals. articles.headline: Liverpool captain Virgil Van Dijk lauds 'outstanding striker' Alexander Isak
articles.description: Liverpool Virgil van Dijk is expecting "fireworks" during Sunday's Merseyside derby and praised the impact of Alexander Isak and Florain Wirtz.
articles.body:
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk is expecting "fireworks" from the first Merseyside derby of the season on Sunday, but on the pitch the pyrotechnics are being supplied by teammates Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz.

Liverpool could cap a significant spell with a third successive victory in eight days and fourth in-a-row after beating Manchester United last weekend and producing a perfect European away performance with a 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge.

Isak (two) and Wirtz scored the goals on freezing night in northern Belgium as their form starts to heat up heading into a pivotal part of the season.

The Sweden international, the club's joint British record signing, took his tally to 10 for the campaign as he became only the eighth player in their history to score in six consecutive away appearances.

Seven goals have come in the last 10 games and it is evident the striker's confidence is blossoming after a frustrating maiden campaign beset by injury but it not just the nature of his strikes -- illustrated by his run and chip over goalkeeper Yann Sommer for the third in Brugge -- which is catching the eye but his all-round contribution to the team.

"Hopefully there are many more goals to come. He's an outstanding striker. On and off the ball he's so important for us. His hold up play was so good, how he carried the ball," Van Dijk said.

"Sometimes when we had to go long, it was difficult for him to win the first ball but he was always there to fight and make it difficult for the defenders.

"It's difficult for me to say [what has changed for Isak] but confidence is massive.

"Staying fit, looking after yourself, knowing what the demands are to be a Liverpool player. Finding your importance in the team helps as well. Alex knows what we need from him and he's delivering that. I think it can only get better from here.

"Everyone has to understand each other's strengths and also sometimes their weaknesses in order to get the best out of each other. The process is going well.

- Liverpool are all smiles as Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak start to click

- Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino

- Iraola: Isak in a 'great moment' after brace vs. Club Brugge

"We are having a great week [but] I expect fireworks on Sunday, given Everton's result in their last game [a 10-man 4-0 defeat at Brentford].

"They are going to come up with a reaction, something comes out of that. You already know that."

Liverpool have won five and lost one of the last cross-city encounters and will make the short trip to Hill Dickinson stadium as favourites, especially after Everton's progress was somewhat abruptly halted by their chastening experience in west London.

Van Dijk scored the winner there in April in the 10th minute of added time and knows their rivals will be out for revenge.

articles.headline: Joshua Kimmich blasts Bayern Munich over Jamal Musiala treatment: 'Absolute no-go'
articles.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.

Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.

Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image.

"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday.

"It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either."

Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition.

"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.

Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension.

Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension.

"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.

Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed.

- Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala mess shows German champs at their worst

- Bayern Munich: Jamal Musiala's health 'top priority' amid contract doubts

- Injury-hit Bayern beaten by Lille to suffer first UCL loss

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue.

Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern.

Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga to Borussia Dortmund and have now slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings.

articles.headline: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
articles.description: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
articles.body:
It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch.

"Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season, while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale.

Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century.

"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%. 

"The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform."

Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate.

Here are the key findings.

Football leads a multisport lineup

 Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports.

Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers."

The generation gap

 The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams.

18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups.

35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each.

articles.headline: Clippers host Pelicans Friday for NBA Cup group stage game
articles.description: New Orleans Pelicans (5-14, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (4-13, 13th in the Western Conference)
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans (5-14, 12th in the Western Conference) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (4-13, 13th in the Western Conference)

Inglewood, California; Friday, 9:30 p.m. EST

BOTTOM LINE: The Los Angeles Clippers take on the New Orleans Pelicans in an NBA Cup in-season tournament group play matchup.

The Clippers are 3-11 in conference matchups. Los Angeles is 1-1 in games decided by less than 4 points.

The Pelicans are 4-11 against Western Conference opponents. New Orleans has a 3-7 record in games decided by 10 or more points.

The Clippers are shooting 45.6% from the field this season, 3.0 percentage points lower than the 48.6% the Pelicans allow to opponents. The Pelicans average 114.5 points per game, 2.9 fewer than the 117.4 the Clippers allow to opponents.

The teams square off for the second time this season. The Clippers won 139-123 in the last meeting on Nov. 9. Darius Garland led the Clippers with 24 points, and Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 26 points.

TOP PERFORMERS: Garland is averaging 20.7 points and 6.4 assists for the Clippers. Brook Lopez is averaging 15.7 points and 5.3 rebounds over the last 10 games.

Zion Williamson is scoring 21.9 points per game and averaging 5.4 rebounds for the Pelicans. Saddiq Bey is averaging 2.6 made 3-pointers over the last 10 games.

LAST 10 GAMES: Clippers: 3-7, averaging 111.1 points, 39.5 rebounds, 26.8 assists, 7.3 steals and 4.8 blocks per game while shooting 46.0% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 118.7 points per game.

Pelicans: 1-9, averaging 109.4 points, 41.4 rebounds, 22.1 assists, 7.7 steals and 4.8 blocks per game while shooting 42.9% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 125.9 points.

INJURIES: Clippers: Jordan Miller: out (shoulder), Bradley Beal: out (knee).

Pelicans: Dejounte Murray: day to day (ankle), Bennedict Mathurin: day to day (plantar), Trendon Watford: day to day (ankle).

articles.description: Denver Nuggets (10-6, seventh in the Western Conference) vs. Utah Jazz (3-16, 14th in the Western Conference)
articles.body:
Denver Nuggets (10-6, seventh in the Western Conference) vs. Utah Jazz (3-16, 14th in the Western Conference)

Salt Lake City; Friday, 9:30 p.m. EST

BOTTOM LINE: The Denver Nuggets visit the Denver Nuggets in an NBA Cup in-season tournament group play matchup.

The Jazz are 3-14 against conference opponents. Utah is 0-2 when it turns the ball over less than its opponents and averages 16.3 turnovers per game.

The Nuggets are 6-6 against Western Conference opponents. Denver has a 3-5 record in games decided by 10 or more points.

The Jazz are shooting 44.7% from the field this season, 2.2 percentage points lower than the 46.9% the Nuggets allow to opponents. The Nuggets average 11.1 made 3-pointers per game this season, 1.3 fewer made shots on average than the 12.4 per game the Jazz give up.
